[BLOCKING] `kitchen_summary` in `orders/reports.py` uses `o.created_at.date()`. That takes the date in whatever time zone the timestamp carries. `london_day`'s docstring says timestamps are UTC and that kitchens report in London time. `daily_revenue` already uses `london_day` for the same grouping.

During British Summer Time (UTC+1), an order created at 23:30 UTC on 2026-06-10 is 00:30 on 06-11 in London. The summary counts it under 06-10, so it lands on the wrong day. The same order is counted under 06-11 by `daily_revenue`. The function returns normally, so nothing flags the mismatch. Orders in the hour after London midnight (00:00–01:00 London) are the ones affected. Their revenue is attributed to the previous day. The two reports will disagree.

Fix: compare `london_day(o.created_at) == day`.
